Bayesian Analysis Using Independent Beta Priors

Source: R/brease.R
brease_ib.Rd

Performs Bayesian analysis of a binary experiment using independent Beta priors on \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_1\). This is a standard conjugate approach for comparison with BREASE.

Usage

brease_ib(
  y0,
  y1,
  N0,
  N1,
  a = c(1, 1),
  b = c(1, 1),
  n_samples = 10000,
  lw = 0.025,
  up = 0.975
)

Arguments

y0

Number of events in the control group.

y1

Number of events in the treatment group.

N0

Number of subjects in the control group.

N1

Number of subjects in the treatment group.

a

Prior shape parameters (vector of length 2 for control and treatment, default c(1, 1)).

b

Prior shape parameters (vector of length 2 for control and treatment, default c(1, 1)).

n_samples

Number of posterior samples (default 10000).

lw

Lower quantile for the credible interval (default 0.025).

up

Upper quantile for the credible interval (default 0.975).

Value

An object of class "brease" (same structure as

brease).

References

Irons, N.J. and Cinelli, C. (2025). Causally Sound Priors for Binary Experiments. Bayesian Analysis. doi:10.1214/25-BA1506

Examples

# Aspirin trial with uniform (flat) prior
result <- brease_ib(y0 = 26, y1 = 10, N0 = 11034, N1 = 11037)
result
#> Bayesian Analysis of Binary Experiment
#> Method: Independent Beta 
#> 
#> Data:
#>   Control:   y0 = 26, N0 = 11034 (rate = 0.0024)
#>   Treatment: y1 = 10, N1 = 11037 (rate = 0.0009)
#> 
#> Prior:
#>   theta0 ~ Beta(1.00, 1.00)
#>   theta1 ~ Beta(1.00, 1.00)
#> 
#> Posterior Summaries:
#>   Baseline Risk (theta0)        Mean: 0.00244  [0.0016, 0.00343]
#>   Treatment Risk (theta1)       Mean: 0.001  [0.000491, 0.00166]
#>   Risk Ratio (RR)               Mean: 0.426  [0.186, 0.797]
#>   Efficacy Fraction (EF)        Mean: 0.574  [0.203, 0.814]
#>   Odds Ratio (OR)               Mean: 0.425  [0.186, 0.797]
#>   Risk Difference (RD)          Mean: -0.00144  [-0.00259, -0.000371]
#> 
#> Bayes Factor (BF10): 0.0493
#> Bayes Factor (BF01): 20.3
